title: Cretan: the dialect of the Erotokritos
lead: Cretan is the dialect you are most likely to hear on a Greek island today, and the one with the richest literature. A Cretan child is a **κοπέλι**, 'now' is **εδά**, and 'what' is **ίντα**; the **κ** of **και** sounds almost like English *ch*. Crete was cut off by Arab rule in the 9th and 10th centuries and then ruled for more than four centuries by Venice, which gave it a Renaissance of its own. Its masterpiece, Kornaros's **Ερωτόκριτος**, is still sung by heart in villages, and its music, the lyra and the improvised **μαντινάδα**, carries the dialect into the present.
facts: Crete, with real differences between east and west (Kontosopoulos's dialect atlas, 1988, maps them). The same southern group includes **Kythera**, Antikythera, **Santorini**, Anafi and **Milos**.
Most of the island's 620,000 people use Cretan features to some degree; the full dialect lives in villages and among older speakers.
The Hellenistic Koine; not the ancient Doric dialect of Crete.
From the 14th century, flourishing 16th–17th c. (the Cretan Renaissance); silent from 1669 until 19th-century collections of folk songs.
About 7,000 Greek-speaking Muslims of Cretan descent in al-Hamidiyah (Syria) and near Tripoli (Lebanon); Cretan Muslims resettled in 1923 at Ayvalık, Cunda and Smyrna.

timeline.text: Crete spoke a **Doric** dialect, known from the Gortyn law code. The Koine replaced it in the Hellenistic period; Cretan descends from that Koine.

Arabs from al-Andalus, after a stay in Egypt, conquer Crete and found an emirate at Chandax (Heraklion). Nikephoros Phokas retakes it in 961. Browning argues that this century and a half of isolation fixed many of Cretan's peculiar features.

**Venetian Crete**. Greek and Venetian live side by side; Venetian loans pour in; Cretan becomes a written literary language: Chortatzis's «Ερωφίλη», the «Θυσία του Αβραάμ», Kornaros's «Ερωτόκριτος» (c. 1600).
Candia falls to the Ottomans after a 21-year siege. Many Cretan writers and scholars flee to the Ionian Islands and Venice, carrying their literature with them.
Ottoman Crete. Many Cretans convert to Islam but keep speaking Cretan Greek. Revolts in 1821, 1866 and 1897 drive Cretan Muslims to emigrate to Syria, Lebanon and Asia Minor.
The autonomous Cretan State; union with Greece in 1913. Cretan Muslims leave in the 1923 exchange.
Standard Greek spreads through school and media; Cretan remains a strong marker of identity, above all in song.

head: Feature
Cretan
Standard
rows: **κ, γ, χ** before **ε, ι** become soft [tɕ, ʑ, ɕ], close to English *ch, j, sh*

sections.after: The soft **κ** is the first thing a mainlander imitates in a Cretan accent.
The future **να πάω θέλω** is a living fossil: medieval Greek formed the future with **θέλω να**, which in the standard shrank to **θα**. Crete kept both words and turned them round.

examples.en: I ask you: the weak pronoun follows the verb.
Make me a coffee: with the object first, the pronoun comes before the imperative.

sections.after: Several of these mean something else in the standard: **πράμα** is 'thing' in Athens and 'nothing' in Crete, as in **«Δεν κατέχω πράμα»** 'I know nothing'; **χτήμα** is 'estate' in Athens and 'donkey' in Crete; **κατέχω** is 'possess' in the standard.

sections.text: Kythera, Antikythera, Santorini, Anafi and Milos share the southern vowel system and many Cretan traits, and the Portal for the Greek Language groups them with Cretan. Kythera, Venetian until 1797 and then part of the Ionian state, also keeps old pronunciations without synizesis.

sample.intro: Vitsentzos Kornaros, c. 1600: 10,012 rhyming fifteen-syllable lines in Cretan. These are lines 1–4 and 41–42, from Stylianos Alexiou's edition; the poem's text is centuries out of copyright.
lines: Του Κύκλου τα γυρίσματα, που ανεβοκατεβαίνουν,
και του Τροχού, που ώρες ψηλά κι ώρες στα βάθη πηαίνουν·
και του Καιρού τα πράματα, που αναπαημό δεν έχουν,
μα στο Καλό κ' εις το Κακό περιπατούν και τρέχουν·
γιατ' ήσαν χρόνους ανταμώς, και τέκνα δεν εκάμα',
σ' έγνοια μεγάλη και βαρά τσ' ήβανε τέτοιο πράμα.
en: The turnings of the Cycle of time, which rise and fall,
and of the Wheel, which now go high and now sink to the depths;
and the things of Time, which know no rest,
but walk and run towards Good and towards Evil.
For they had been together for years and had no children,
and this had put them into great and heavy worry.
sample.source: Βιτσέντζος Κορνάρος, Ερωτόκριτος, Α΄ 1–4, 41–42, ed. Στ. Αλεξίου (1980).

culture.text: In Crete, feelings are still put into **μαντινάδες**: rhyming couplets of fifteen-syllable lines, improvised at weddings and feasts to the **λύρα** and **λαούτο**, or texted to a sweetheart. The great performers, such as Nikos Xylouris and Psarantonis, made Cretan known all over Greece, and every Cretan knows a few lines of «Ερωτόκριτος» set to music.

questions.why: Cretan forms its future with **θέλω** after the verb, a reversed form of medieval **θέλω να**.

questions.q: What made Cretan a written literary language?
options: Venetian rule and the Cretan Renaissance
questions.answer: Venetian rule and the Cretan Renaissance
questions.why: 16th–17th-century Venetian Crete produced Erotokritos, Erofili and other works.
τ before ι + vowel becomes θ.

questions.q: Where is Cretan still spoken outside Greece?
questions.why: Descendants of Cretan Muslims who left between 1866 and 1897.
